stimulus.text: Paraphrase: In December 1944, German forces made one last desperate attack in the Ardennes region of Belgium, pushing a bulge into the Allied lines in what became known as the Battle of the Bulge. American counterattacks under General George S. Patton halted the advance, at a cost of more than 85,000 American troops killed, wounded, or captured. In the spring of 1945, Allied troops crossed the Rhine in March, and Soviet troops stormed Berlin in April. Hitler killed himself on April 30, and Germany surrendered on May 8, 1945, a day celebrated as V-E Day, Victory in Europe Day.
stimulus.source_note: Original secondary summary drawn from 5 Steps Chapter 24 (Battle of the Bulge; 85,000 American casualties; Rhine March 1945; Hitler's suicide April 30; surrender May 8, V-E Day) and Barron's Chapter 9.

source: original; stimulus drawn from book-grounded figures and paraphrases (see source_note)
stem: The passage describes a German attack in December 1944 that pushed a bulge into Allied lines. What was that battle called?

options.misconception: Midway was a naval battle in the Pacific in June 1942.

options.text: The Battle of the Coral Sea
options.misconception: The Coral Sea was a naval battle in the Pacific in May 1942.
Leyte Gulf was a naval battle in the Philippines in October 1944.

rationales.A: Midway was a Pacific naval battle in June 1942.
rationales.B: The Coral Sea was a Pacific naval battle in May 1942.
rationales.C: The passage names the December 1944 attack in Belgium the Battle of the Bulge.
rationales.D: Leyte Gulf was a Pacific naval battle in October 1944.
rationales.general:
1. The passage places the attack in Belgium in December 1944.
2. It says German forces pushed a bulge into the Allied lines.
3. That shape gave the battle its name: the Battle of the Bulge.
4. The other choices are all Pacific naval battles, fought at sea.
Remember: a battle's nickname often describes its shape, so match the name to the picture.
